scope: Only the existing four uniswap-v3 original SwapRouter roots (1/10/137/42161), seven uniswap-v3-router02 roots (1/10/56/137/143/8453/42161), and six sushiswap-v3 direct SwapRouter roots (1/10/56/137/8453/42161). Exhaust ordinary fixed financial settlement/funding and structured fixed-source liquidity helpers. No new protocol, deployed root, Sushi position manager, approval, permit, generic executor/callback, runtime, profile, grant or multicall scope expansion.

priorEvidence: sources/uniswap-execution-support.json (V4/Universal Router evidence is not substituted for these V3 roots)
reviewBasis.admission: Contract-first finite exact-target inventory. Permissionless ordinary whole-balance recovery is financial functionality, not an independent opaque-execution boundary. No private-escrow, financial-cap, owner-only, health, funding, execution, runtime-persistence or safety assurance is invented.
reviewBasis.supersession: The complete function decisions here supersede historical whole-balance helper exclusions at these exact roots. Historical exclusions of approvals/permits/opaque calls/callbacks remain. Existing functions keep exact IDs/ABIs/operations/scopes; existingFunctionUpdates only revises obsolete warning copy.
reviewBasis.executionBoundary: Direct fixed ABI functions are standalone capabilities only. No allowedChildren entry, executionScope, profile, API-key grant, calldata language or nested-execution authorization is added or broadened. A generic callPositionManager(bytes) stays excluded even though structured mint/increaseLiquidity internally construct its fixed calldata.
reviewBasis.limitations: Retained/fresh source evidence is not current runtime bytecode identity, balances, allowance sufficiency, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or deployment persistence. Sourcify match grades and Monad explorer similar match are retained without upgrades.

Ordinary direct financial method, not private escrow: router native/ERC20 balances are shared custody, not deposits attributed to this caller. Permissionless refund/sweep/unwrap can recover whole balances, and another account can recover stranded funds first; separate funding and settlement transactions expose balances to loss.

All these ABI methods are payable. msg.value is native currency of this chain despite ETH/WETH9 names. Except wrapETH, these helpers do not automatically wrap supplied native value; supplied value can remain on the router unless refundETH sends it out. Prefer zero native value unless deliberately required; no automatic refund guarantee.

Caller selects tokens, recipient/fee recipient, amounts and minimums where exposed. Permissionless refund/sweep/unwrap can recover whole balances, and another account can recover stranded funds first; separate funding and settlement transactions expose balances to loss.

All these ABI methods are payable. msg.value is native currency of this chain despite ETH/WETH9 names. Prefer zero native value unless deliberately required; no automatic refund guarantee.

Caller selects tokens, recipient/fee recipient, amounts and minimums where exposed. Fee-on-transfer/rebasing/nonstandard tokens, receiver behavior, rounding and external dependencies can revert or change financial outcomes.

Use the intended ordinary nonzero recipient, not a router-custody sentinel.

Router02 V2 path is an explicit token-address array, not arbitrary execution data. Every pair is derived by CREATE2 from immutable factoryV2 0x5c69bee701ef814a2b6a3edd4b1652cb9cc5aa6f and the source-fixed Uniswap V2 init-code hash; pair.swap receives empty callback bytes. This inventory does not establish pair existence or live liquidity on every route.

Exact-input V2 consumes amountIn and checks the recipient balance increase against amountOutMin. This loop supports fee-on-transfer inputs/outputs through balance deltas but token taxes/nonstandard transfers remain risks. amountIn=0 is CONTRACT_BALANCE and swaps the router entire input-token balance rather than a zero caller amount; avoid this sentinel for caller-funded swaps.

## Uniswap v3 Staker

An up-to-date list of [deploy addresses by chain is hosted on GitHub](https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-staker/releases/tag/v1.0.2) for the `UniswapV3Staker` contract.

## Universal Router

The `UniversalRouter` contract is the current preferred entrypoint for ERC20 and NFT swaps, replacing, among other contracts, `SwapRouter02`. An up-to-date list of [deploy addresses by chain is hosted on GitHub](https://github.com/Uniswap/universal-router/tree/main/deploy-addresses).

## Uniswap Pool Deployments

Every Uniswap pool is a unique instance of the `UniswapV3Pool` contract and is deployed at its own unique address. The contract source code of the pool will be auto-verified on etherscan. For example, here is the [ETH/USDC 0.3% pool](https://etherscan.io/address/0x8ad599c3a0ff1de082011efddc58f1908eb6e6d8) on Ethereum mainnet.

You can look up the address of an existing pool on [Uniswap Info](https://info.uniswap.org/#/) or by calling the `getPool` function on the `UniswapV3Factory` contract.

```solidity
getPool("0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48", "0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2", 3000)
```

## Wrapped Native Token Addresses

The Uniswap Protocol supports trading of ERC20 tokens. In order to swap a native asset like ETH (or MATIC on Polygon), the Uniswap protocol wraps these assets in an ERC20 wrapped native token contract. The protocol uses the following WETH9 addresses on Ethereum and WMATIC addresses on Polygon.

| Network             | ChainId     | Wrapped Native Token | Address                                      |
| ------------------- | ----------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Ethereum            | `1`         | WETH                 | `0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2` |
| Sepolia             | `11155111`  | WETH                 | `0xfff9976782d46cc05630d1f6ebab18b2324d6b14` |

## Uniswap v3 Staker

An up-to-date list of [deploy addresses by chain is hosted on GitHub](https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-staker/releases/tag/v1.0.2) for the `UniswapV3Staker` contract.

## Universal Router

The `UniversalRouter` contract is the current preferred entrypoint for ERC20 and NFT swaps, replacing, among other contracts, `SwapRouter02`. An up-to-date list of [deploy addresses by chain is hosted on GitHub](https://github.com/Uniswap/universal-router/tree/main/deploy-addresses).

## Uniswap Pool Deployments

Every Uniswap pool is a unique instance of the `UniswapV3Pool` contract and is deployed at its own unique address. The contract source code of the pool will be auto-verified on etherscan. For example, here is the [ETH/USDC 0.3% pool](https://etherscan.io/address/0x8ad599c3a0ff1de082011efddc58f1908eb6e6d8) on Ethereum mainnet.

You can look up the address of an existing pool on [Uniswap Info](https://info.uniswap.org/#/) or by calling the `getPool` function on the `UniswapV3Factory` contract.

```solidity
getPool("0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48", "0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2", 3000)
```

## Wrapped Native Token Addresses

The Uniswap Protocol supports trading of ERC20 tokens. In order to swap a native asset like ETH (or MATIC on Polygon), the Uniswap protocol wraps these assets in an ERC20 wrapped native token contract. The protocol uses the following WETH9 addresses on Ethereum and WMATIC addresses on Polygon.

| Network             | ChainId  | Wrapped Native Token | Address                                      |
| ------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Base                | `8453`   | WETH                 | `0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006` |
| Base Sepolia        | `84532`  | WETH                 | `0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006` |
